title: Order cancellation across controller, service, and repository layers
name: Order cancellation endpoints

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how responsibilities are split between the HTTP routes, the service, and the repository? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
In OrderService.placeOrder, what happens if the second line's SKU cannot be reserved?
choices: The first line's reservation stays in place and the order is inserted with only one line
OutOfStockError is thrown inside the transaction, so the first reservation is rolled back and no order is inserted
The order is inserted with status pending and the missing stock is back-ordered
The route returns 409 because the error handler maps OutOfStockError

questions.prompt: Why does OrderService.cancelOrder load the order with findByIdForUpdate instead of findById?
choices: findById does not map snake_case columns to the Order shape
findByIdForUpdate caches the row for the rest of the request
It locks the order row in the transaction so a concurrent status change cannot slip in between the check and the update
FOR UPDATE is required for any SELECT that is later followed by an UPDATE in Postgres

questions.prompt: Which layer in this code is responsible for translating domain errors like InvalidOrderStateError into HTTP status codes?
choices: The router's error-handling middleware in orderRoutes.ts
OrderService, which throws errors carrying status codes
OrderRepository, which inspects database error codes
Express's default error handler, which reads the error class name
